classification.difficultyReason: Interpret every third station as increments of three from station 1, then represent the resulting stops on an equally spaced number line.

content.prompt: The manager of an underground railway system decides to save time in the mornings by having one particular train only stop at every third station between stations 1 and 19, starting at station 1. The stations are all 1 km apart. Show the stations on a number line and mark with a dot each station where the train stops.

answer.worked: Draw equally spaced ticks labelled 1 to 19, with each interval representing 1 km. Starting at station 1, count three intervals to each next stop. Mark dots at stations $1, 4, 7, 10, 13, 16, 19$.

spec.sourceRegion: Exercise 1A, question 3; answer figure on teacher PDF page 1
spec.description: Equally spaced stations labelled 1–19, with black stop dots at every third interval starting at station 1.
spec.mathematics: Consecutive station positions differ by 1 km; consecutive stops differ by three station intervals.
